summary: The 1918 Kempshall Mountain fire tower was dismantled; the Adirondack History Museum rebuilt one tower from its parts and West Mountain parts, NHLR-registered 2022.

facts.design: Single tower rebuilt from portions of the Kempshall Mountain tower (35-foot Aermotor LS40, 1918) and the West Mountain tower
facts.status_note: The standing tower is the museum rebuild; the Kempshall Mountain tower itself was dismantled

access.note: Climb is inside the museum; museum open Wednesday to Saturday 10 AM to 4 PM and Sundays 12 PM to 4 PM, from Memorial Day weekend to Columbus Day weekend

visit.trail_note: Visitors enter the Adirondack History Museum in Elizabethtown to climb the tower

events.note: First structure on the mountain: a wooden tower built by the Conservation Commission
Wooden tower replaced by a 35-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower
Fire lookout operations ended at the end of the 1971 season as aerial detection took over
The Explorer says the steel tower was dismantled in June 1977; the NHLR entry says the Kempshall and West towers were removed in the 1980s
NHLR says the museum bought the tower parts and built a single tower in the 1990s; 1990 is the start of that decade, not a confirmed date
Registered May 22, 2022 as US 1596, NY 48; nominated by Laurie Rankin

corrections.current: Kempshall Mountain Lookout (now at the Adirondack History Museum)
corrections.proposed: Adirondack History Museum Fire Tower (rebuilt from parts of the Kempshall Mountain and West Mountain towers)
corrections.why: The NHLR entry and the FFLOS list describe one museum tower rebuilt from Kempshall and West parts in the 1990s; the Kempshall Mountain tower itself was dismantled, so the name suggests more continuity than there is.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Adirondack Explorer gives June 1977 for dismantling the steel tower. The NHLR entry says the Kempshall and West towers were removed in the 1980s. Wikipedia gives no removal date. The story reports the disagreement and uses the Explorer's specific date.

Wikipedia calls the Elizabethtown museum the Essex County Historical Museum. The museum's events page and the NHLR entry use Adirondack History Museum. The story uses the museum's own name and mentions the Wikipedia name.

Wikipedia places the mountain northwest of the hamlet of Long Lake. The Explorer says it is on the northeast side of Long Lake. The story avoids the direction and says only that it is near the hamlet.

notes_for_editor: Removal date conflicts (1977 vs 1980s) and the mountain's direction from Long Lake conflict; see resolved_conflicts. The 1911 wooden tower and 1918 date rest mainly on Wikipedia, which cites a New York fire-lookout list that was not read. The Explorer profile is long; only the opening and the early history passage were read. The 1990s rebuild and the 2022 registration rest on the NHLR entry alone. Museum hours come from the museum homepage and may change seasonally. Brief record corrected: the museum tower is a rebuild from Kempshall and West parts, so the name is corrected. No photos added. Not verified: whether climbing is allowed on every open day. Check 2026-10-09: all 22 quotes were found on the first run; four footnoted claims were corrected (beside to near the hamlet, summit to mountain for the 1911 tower, Wikipedia 'says only' overstatement, and the missing footnote for the single exhibit tower) and the undated 'Today' hours claim now attributes the hours to the museum homepage.
